new_jobs.description:
Job Description

What if you could do the kind of work the world needs?

At WSP, you can access our global scale, contribute to landmark projects and connect with the brightest minds in your field to do the best work of your life. You can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates new ideas and diverse perspectives. You can experience a world of opportunity and the chance to shape a career as unique as you

We're looking for an Environmental Scientist
to join our Contaminated Land Management (CLM) team
in Sydney. This is an exciting opportunity to work on diverse contaminated land and groundwater projects across New South Wales and nationally, helping clients understand, manage and remediate environmental risks. The role is suited to an environmental professional with at least 2 years' commercial experience
who is looking to build technical expertise, strengthen project delivery skills and take the next step in their consulting career.

As part of our established multidisciplinary Environment business, you'll collaborate with experienced contaminated land specialists, geologists, hydrogeologists and environmental engineers to deliver innovative solutions for site investigation, environmental due diligence, risk assessment and remediation projects. Our work spans mining, petroleum-contaminated land, industrial facilities and government assets, supporting the rehabilitation and redevelopment of complex sites.

This role offers a balance of fieldwork, technical reporting, project coordination and client engagement, providing exposure to a broad range of challenging and rewarding contaminated land projects.

About The Role

As an Environmental Scientist
, you'll play a key role in delivering contaminated land investigations and remediation projects while developing your technical and project management capabilities. You'll work closely with experienced consultants and project managers, contributing to high-quality client outcomes across a variety of sectors.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Conducting contaminated land and groundwater investigations, including soil, groundwater and vapour sampling programs.
Coordinating fieldwork activities, contractors and subcontractors to ensure safe, compliant and high-quality project delivery.
Interpreting environmental data and developing conceptual site models.
Preparing technical reports, environmental assessments and remediation documentation.
Assisting with project coordination, including budgets, schedules, scope and stakeholder communication.
Applying environmental legislation, standards and contaminated land guidelines to project delivery.
Contributing to proposal preparation and supporting business development opportunities.
Mentoring graduates and supporting a strong culture of safety, quality and technical excellence.

About You

We're seeking an environmental professional who combines strong technical skills with a passion for contaminated land management and delivering exceptional client outcomes.

You Will Bring

Bachelor's degree in Earth Sciences, Environmental Engineering or equivalent.
At least 2+ years’ experience in contaminated land assessment, remediation or environmental consulting.
Experience undertaking contaminated land and groundwater investigations and field programs.
Understanding of contaminated land legislation, standards and regulatory frameworks.
Strong data interpretation and technical report writing skills.
Ability to coordinate multiple project tasks while maintaining quality, safety and budget requirements.
Experience supervising contractors, subcontractors or junior team members.
Excellent communication skills and a collaborative approach to working with clients and colleagues.
Commitment to safety, innovation, quality and technical excellence.

Why WSP?

At WSP, we value our people and our reputation. We are locally dedicated with international scale, future-focused, collaborative and empowering — and we’re looking for people who share those values.

You’ll be part of a team that delivers technical excellence while keeping client outcomes, sustainability, quality and safety at the centre of what we do. You’ll also have the opportunity to grow your leadership capability, contribute to meaningful projects and help shape better outcomes for communities and clients.

Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all.

Join our close-knit community of talented individuals who share your passion for making a positive impact.

With us, you can. Apply today.

new_jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Do you like working with different project teams in a fast-paced environment? Are you interested in joining an organization focused on making a positive impact? If so, we’d like to talk with you about growing with us.

EnSafe is seeking a full-time Environmental Scientist/Project Manager to join our team of professionals at our San Diego, CA, office.

This position has a requirement to work onsite, at the office, if needed relocation assistance may be offered to meet this expectation.

What We Are Looking For

An Environmental Scientist with proven experience managing environmental due diligence projects and a strong ability to translate complex findings into clear, defensible Phase I ESA reports. You’ll work with clients across California and beyond, managing projects from site assessment through final reporting while gaining exposure to Phase II investigations, environmental sampling, and emerging areas such as PFAS risk evaluation.

Joining our team means immersing yourself in an environment that nurtures creativity, encourages collaboration at all levels, fosters a supportive culture, and facilitates professional development.

Key responsibilities of this position include

What You Will Be Doing

Perform and manage Phase I Environmental Site Assessments in accordance with ASTM and applicable regulatory requirements.
Conduct site reconnaissance, historical research, regulatory database review, interviews, and other due diligence activities.
Prepare clear, technically sound Phase I ESA reports and recommendations.
Manage multiple Phase I ESA projects, including scope, schedule, budget, subcontractors, client communication, and deliverables.
Provide technical and peer review of Phase I ESA reports as experience permits.
Support Phase II environmental site investigations and other due diligence activities when warranted.
Plan and conduct environmental sampling activities involving soil, groundwater, soil vapor, indoor air, surface water, or other environmental media.
Prepare work plans, technical memoranda, investigation reports, and proposals.
Communicate findings and environmental risk considerations clearly to clients and project teams.
Coordinate work with junior staff and provide technical guidance and mentoring.
Support environmental compliance projects based on experience and workload, which may include hazardous materials and hazardous waste management, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, EPCRA/Tier II, or related regulatory requirements.
Participate in business development activities, including preparation of scopes, budgets, proposals, and support for existing client relationships.
Travel periodically to project sites throughout California and as needed, elsewhere in the United States.

Minimum Skills And Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, Geology, Environmental Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering discipline.
Approximately 6 or more years of relevant environmental consulting experience.
Demonstrated experience preparing Phase I Environmental Site Assessments.
Strong technical writing and report preparation skills.
Ability to independently conduct site reconnaissance and evaluate environmental conditions.
Working knowledge of environmental due diligence practices and applicable federal and state environmental regulations.

new_jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

The Drinking Water Market Sector (“MS”) Business Development Director (BDD) will lead the development and implementation of business strategies across all HDR geographies in coordination with Market Sector and Regional Business Group leadership, operational leadership, client managers and Business Class Directors.   Reporting to the Director of Market Sector Development, and in full coordination with the Water Business Group leadership, the Drinking Water BDD creates and monitors frequent and regular communication across the Sector to drive top-line NFB growth and to implement the Drinking Water sector’s strategic initiatives, growth plans and marketing opportunities for the market sector. This market leader will support and collaborate across all HDR market sectors, regions, areas and business lines to advance a variety of strategies intended to grow services across the market sector. 

Drinking Water Market Sector–
Within the Water Business Group, the Drinking Water MS is a highly technical and diversified sector.  This reflects that this service offering routinely works for local municipalities, private entities, distinct water utilities, Federal, regional and local governments, and similar clients in each of the 50 US states, Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia.  In 2026 Engineering News Record ranked HDR fifth in size of business in the important water supply and treatment category.  We have over 475 employees in this MS spanning the range of services from utility master planning, program management, strategic advisory services, transmission and distribution, water supply management, water treatment and reuse, construction management and inspection, and asset management and operations assistance.

The Drinking Water MS is comprised of a multi-layer organization to drive business and client development, while at the same time defining and implementing strategic drinking water initiatives for growth, coordinating best practices and quality professional services, and projecting the HDR brand in the marketplace.  Specific attention is required to capture the potential of the wide spectrum of employees throughout the Sector, while at the same time developing and reinforcing the image of HDR with our clients across the various drinking water markets.  

Business Development Responsibilities
 – The Drinking Water Market Sector BDD primary performance metric is achieving NFB goals for the sector. You will provide leadership and substantial support to assessing the Regional and Area marketplace positioning and determining optimal technical strategies needed to win and secure contracts and expand business. Business development efforts will extend across all business groups to coordinate with other Architecture, Transportation, Resources, Water, BES and Federal Business Group market sectors.  This position will implement cross sector initiatives including One Water, the Value of Water, and other Sector strategies that are effective in gaining market share, and that will successfully interface with Regional/Area client development programs, our Strategic Pursuits program, and Regional/Area marketing managers/pursuit leaders. Specific business development activities include:

Incorporate our HDR and Water business vision within the market sector to become the industry leader.

Serve as the Client Manager for selected key clients within the Sector and be active and visible in the industry.

Serve as Pursuit Leader on select drinking water opportunities, leading by example in the development of pursuit strategies, proposal development and interview preparation.

Work with client managers to promote the marketing and delivery of all HDR services to Drinking Water clients across all HDR geographies.

Participate as a member of the Water Business Group Management and the National Drinking Water Market Sector Leadership Team support the coordinated development of international markets in Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia, in support of broader Water Business Group international growth initiatives. Work with Regional Business Group Managers and Client Development Leadership in the development and delivery of MS initiatives that align with area and regional drivers.

Work with the client development leaders to support client development, deploy pursuit strategies, and guide pursuit processes, based on proven capture techniques.

Provide direct support to selected pursuits through client relationship development and/or through development of strategy, technical differentiation, and participation in related pursuit activities.

Actively participate in industry associations in leadership roles and serve as a company role-model in business and community organizations.

Identify key investments (acquisitions and technology) that will maintain or drive HDR into an industry leadership position.

Maintain awareness of Area marketing capabilities and provide market sector support to Areas toward achieving Drinking Water MS booking goals. 

Develop relationships with industry counterparts in other consulting and construction organizations. 

Develop relationships with senior leadership in key client organizations.

Staff Development Responsibilities
 – The Drinking Water MS BDD will seek opportunities to enhance our performance to win new work within the marketplace and provide opportunities for staff growth and development.  Through pursuit leadership and involvement, strategically align Drinking Water staff and projects to develop and deepen skills, while mentoring and growing their capabilities and talent. Lead and/or assist with the identification and recruitment of prospective future market sector employees.

Work with the Drinking Water MS leader, Business Class Directors, and practice groups to drive technical excellence and coordinate technical staff to promote quality delivery and our Drive to Zero initiative. 

Coordinate staffing/recruiting plans for key hires and assist local leadership as necessary with local hires. Identify resource gaps and support talent management and recruiting.

Support to Key Project/Program Delivery –
 The Drinking Water MS BDD will assist Regional and Area Business Group leadership in key project delivery within the market sector.  Key responsibilities consist of helping to drive client management, acting as Principal in Charge on key project delivery, and supporting the QA/QC program to provide for successful project delivery. Facilitate cooperation and eliminate hurdles and barriers to success. Work with a business group leadership to implement process improvements and leverage work sharing to meet or exceed planned goals.

Be aware of staff workload and facilitate work sharing within the market sector; promote effective use of company resources and assist in applying key staff/expertise to projects. 

Assist with contract review on key projects to help ensure risk management, proper staffing, quality reviews and resolution of claims.

Take on Principal in Charge assignments that leverage this leadership role by driving client satisfaction, staff development, technical excellence and mentoring opportunities.

Preferred Qualifications

Minimum 20 + years of experience in drinking water planning and engineering design, client development, and project management; much of that experience must reside within servicing of drinking water public and private clients and utilities.
Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in an accredited civil or environmental engineering program.
Maintain a professional engineering registration.
Experienced in development and management of strategic positioning and technical differentiation for planning and/or engineering services.
Experienced in development and management of a wide range of client relationships and specific program and/or project pursuits.
Experienced in overall staff development to include recruiting, career path development, and professional growth.
Experienced with industry associations and maintains an active and visible profile in the market sector.
Ability to work cooperatively with Market Sector Directors, Business Class Directors, Regional Business Group Director, Area Business Group Managers, Area Marketing Managers and Area Manager.
Demonstrated commitment to HDR values. An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must.

Required Qualifications

A minimum of 15 years relevant industry experience
Demonstrated "self-starter" with a history of completing projects with limited oversight
Deep knowledge of the A/E/C industry's standard approach to procurement of professional services
Demonstrated ability to motivate and inspire others
Demonstrated ability to build a network of clients and industry partners
Experience in sales and developing effective win strategies
Strong financial acumen and negotiation skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Ability and desire to travel and engage with others in-person
Demonstrated experience in growing programs in new or highly competitive markets
Demonstrated experience in winning high-value contracts in the A/E/C industry
Demonstrated experience in writing compelling content based on information from technical staff

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee ownership, employee health, performance, and success, which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time away, parental leave, paid holidays, a retirement savings plan with employer match, employee referral bonus and tuition reimbursement. The expected compensation range for this position is $176,000 - $315,000 depending upon skills, experience, education and geographical location. (Stated benefits are for full-time regular positions. Position Purpose

Associate Environmental Scientists use their species specific and relevant environmental knowledge to provide important services pertaining to the health of communities and work to protect the environment from serious hazards. This position is a professional position with responsibility for gathering, compiling, analyzing, and interpreting complex data, then utilizing the information to prepare technical documents and presentations, with an emphasis on NEPA and CEQA compliance. This position is one of a team member who works with general direction from his/her supervisor and expresses a higher level of independence than an Assistant Environmental Scientist by performing more complex tasks with less direct oversight. The Associate Environment Scientist will assist in routine to moderately complex environmental assessment and remediation projects. This includes the assessment of the risks of new construction to the environment that is needed in order to complete our projects.

Essential Tasks And Responsibilities

Conduct field surveys for threatened, endangered, or rare species, as well as species’ habitat in support of ESA, CWA, Section 404, and other environmental regulations
Observe and monitor species in the field
Conduct archival / electronic research with USFWS and other state and federal agencies
Conduct land use / development monitoring for natural / biological resources protection
Assure permits are requested and maintained appropriately
Provide input for those sections of NEPA and CEQA documents pertaining to environment and data collection methodology
Prepare leave in technical memoranda, meeting minutes, transmittals, presentations, and other written materials
Assist senior staff with presentations to public agencies and clients
Assist with teaching junior staff
Compile data and information for public presentations
Other duties as assigned or as needed in order to successfully complete project deliverables or meet internal goals

Essential Skills And Abilities

Species identification and research / survey, vegetation community and habitat classification and inventory, monitoring, data synthesis and interpretations required
Ability to develop creative solutions to project issues
Ability to take direction and use initiative to complete tasks without direct supervision
Ability to organize, collect and analyze data, generate and evaluate alternatives, reach logical conclusions, and formulate consistent recommendations as necessary
Proficient in MS Word and Excel
Quantitative analysis skills
Ability to work in a team environment
Critical thinking skills
Technical writing skills
Ability to sit and stand for long periods
Strong ability to communicate well (in writing and verbally) with other staff, clients, and agencies to accomplish team goals
Visual acuity and manual dexterity
Ability to perform repetitive wrist and hand motions required
Ability to travel to field sites and walk long distances may be required on occasion

Education

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in biology, botany, wildlife management, ecology, environmental biology, or environmental science

Experience

Two (2) to five (5) years’ experience (or MA/MS and one (1) years of experience), especially in the areas of NEPA and CEQA compliance, wetlands delineations, CWA, ESA, and related federal and/or state environmental compliance regulations. Field experience in California or with CA species preferred.

Organizational Relationships

The Associate Environmental Scientist provides support to all members of the environmental scientist group, as well as the planning group. Assistant Environmental Scientists are assigned to a Team/Group Leader for managerial purposes but will also receive guidance and direction from the discipline’s Technical Leader. The Associate Environmental Scientist is encouraged to create a mentor/protégé relationship with one or more senior members of the bio team and may be asked to act as a Teaming Advisor for junior staff. Associate Environmental Scientists are expected to work with both planning and bio team members throughout the entire firm in order to promote our “One Company” philosophy.

About The Role

The City of Bend is accepting applications for one (1) regular, full-time Environmental Compliance Analyst in the Environmental Services Division of the Water Services Department. This is a COBEA represented, non-exempt (overtime-eligible) position. This position will be open until filled and may be used to create an eligibility list for future vacancies. Please review the entire job posting, including the application requirements at the end.

This role is all about helping the City understand what’s happening across its water systems, whether that’s drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, or local rivers and groundwater. On any given day, you might be out in the field collecting water samples, checking monitoring equipment, or downloading flow data from sites across the City. Other days may involve reviewing and validating that data, troubleshooting equipment issues, or helping respond to unusual conditions such as storm events. In simple terms, this position helps answer critical questions: Is our water safe? Are our systems functioning properly? Are we meeting environmental regulations?

This position offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of environmental science, public health, and infrastructure. Current and upcoming projects include expanding the City’s flow monitoring network and supporting the installation of new real-time level sensors that help detect and prevent system overflows. The role also contributes to groundwater and surface water monitoring, evolving regulatory compliance efforts, and improved data-driven decision-making.

This position plays a key support role across several City programs, including Industrial Pretreatment, Stormwater, Wastewater, Drinking Water, and Engineering. The data collected and analyzed directly informs engineering models, regulatory compliance, infrastructure investment decisions, and environmental protection efforts—making this an essential role in advancing the City’s mission to protect public health and the environment.

Classification Framework:
Environmental Compliance Analyst

What You'll Do

The following duties are a sample of major duties performed in this role and not intended to be an exhaustive list:

Conduct flow monitoring activities including field equipment maintenance, sensor replacement, and data validation
Collect water samples across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, groundwater, and surface water systems
Calibrate and maintain analytical instruments and monitoring equipment to ensure accurate data collection
Perform stormwater and environmental sampling during qualifying weather or system events
Monitor and sample permitted industrial dischargers to ensure regulatory compliance
Analyze, interpret, and summarize environmental and operational data for reports and decision-making
Prepare technical reports, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and monitoring plans
Support biosolids, groundwater, and wastewater treatment facility monitoring programs
Troubleshoot mechanical and technical issues in field instrumentation and monitoring systems
Maintain compliance with safety protocols, including confined space entry, hazardous materials handling, and traffic control

Ideal Candidate

We’re looking for someone who is a self-starter, detail-oriented, and comfortable balancing multiple priorities in a dynamic environment. The ideal candidate enjoys hands-on, field-based work and can adapt to changing conditions while maintaining a high level of accuracy and safety. They bring a proactive approach to problem-solving and take initiative in maintaining and improving systems and processes.

Highly qualified candidates will have working knowledge of environmental monitoring practices, water and wastewater systems, and regulatory compliance requirements. They bring strong skills in data analysis, technical troubleshooting, and clear communication—both written and verbal. The ability to interpret data, identify anomalies, and connect findings to system performance is critical to success in this role.

Candidates who meet the listed minimum qualifications, including an equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered for an interview. Please ensure your application includes information about your education, relevant paid and unpaid work experience, and applicable licenses and certifications. Avoid referencing your resume in the job duties section of the application.

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, engineering, chemistry, biology, or a related field; AND
Experience: Relevant experience in environmental monitoring, water quality, wastewater/stormwater systems, or related technical field; OR
An equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the job

Required Licenses & Certifications

Valid Oregon Driver’s License (or ability to obtain by date of hire)

Desired (but not required) Attributes

Experience with environmental sampling and laboratory procedures
Familiarity with EPA, DEQ, or other regulatory frameworks
Experience working with field instrumentation or monitoring equipment
Knowledge of data management, analysis tools, or reporting systems
Experience in municipal or public sector utilities

Environmental Scientist/Industrial Hygienist

Apex is seeking an environmental professional with experience in industrial hygiene to perform asbestos, lead-paint, mold/moisture intrusion, exposure assessment, abatement monitoring, and related industrial hygiene and EHS compliance projects across Southern California.

Employee Benefits

This role offers competitive compensation and a robust benefits package, a balanced mix of fieldwork and report writing, company sponsorship for professional and vocational training, work from home opportunity, collaboration with other industrial hygiene, EHS and other experts, and continued professional development and growth afforded by a rapidly growing national environmental consulting company.

Key Responsibilities

Perform asbestos, lead-based paint (LBP), and microbial/moisture intrusion assessments, along with abatement oversight, with an approximate 50/50 split between field and office work

Support additional environmental services through cross-training, including:
Exposure assessments
Workplace safety evaluations
Stormwater compliance inspections
Soil and groundwater sampling
Noise and air monitoring
Aboveground Storage Tank (AST) inspections

Execute work in alignment with project work plans, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and direction from project managers
Manage scheduling and logistics across all project phases, from coordination and fieldwork through reporting
Prepare clear, accurate, and technically sound client-ready reports using project-specific templates
Collaborate with internal teams to support project delivery and ongoing professional development
Maintain and proactively pursue relevant certifications, including 40-Hour HAZWOPER, CAC, and/or CSST

2+ years of professional experience conducting asbestos surveys and mold/moisture intrusion inspections as an AHERA-accredited inspector (in any state)

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Microbiology, or a related field

Strong technical writing and critical thinking skills

Excellent attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate in a team-oriented environment

Commitment to safety and a strong understanding of safe work practices
Interest in growing within industrial hygiene and expanding into broader environmental consulting services

Company-subsidized medical and dental.
Company-paid life, short, and long-term disability.
401k match, tuition assistance, and more.
Cross-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.
Performance-based bonuses or other incentives.
Working with the best and brightest in the industry.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Who are we looking for?

GHD is seeking a dedicated and knowledgeable Environmental Staff Scientist
to join our dynamic team in one of the following offices: Sacramento, Roseville, Concord, CA
. In this Environmental Professional role, you will play a key part in supporting environmental assessments, regulatory compliance, site investigations, and sustainable project development across a diverse range of industries. The ideal candidate will bring a solid foundation in environmental science, geology, or engineering, proven field and analytical skills, and a passion for applying scientific principles to real-world environmental challenges. This position is an integral part of our contamination assessment and remediation (CAR) business group and requires a diverse array of responsibilities.

As part of our interdisciplinary team, you will contribute to impactful projects involving environmental investigation, remediation, and risk assessment, while working closely with clients, regulatory agencies, and internal stakeholders. This is an exciting opportunity for a mid-level professional looking to expand their career in a collaborative, mission-driven environment. You’ll work alongside industry experts and mentors who are invested in your professional development, with access to ongoing training, leadership opportunities, and a clear path toward advancement. Strong communication skills, a proactive mindset, and a commitment to environmental stewardship are essential to succeed in this role. Whether you’re looking to deepen your technical expertise or broaden your impact across multidisciplinary projects, we offer the support and resources to help you take the next step in your environmental science career.

Our Hybrid Work Model
Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in office, three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Data Collection and Analysis: Collate and analyze data using preset tools, methods, and formats. Involves working independently.
Personal Capability Building: Develop own capabilities by participating in assessment and development planning activities as well as formal and informal training and coaching; gain or maintain external professional accreditation, where relevant, to improve performance and fulfill personal potential. Maintain an understanding of relevant technology, external regulation, and industry best practices through ongoing education, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
Health, Safety, and Environment: Follow the organization's health, safety, and environment (HSE) policies, procedures, and mandatory instructions to identify and mitigate environmental risks and risks to the well-being of self and others in the workplace. Identify patterns of risky behavior within the team and take appropriate action to resolve them, escalating serious issues as appropriate.
Client & Customer Management (External): Manage relationships with small clients while also helping senior colleagues manage relationships with larger key clients and customers.
Sampling and Testing: Collect a range of samples for laboratory testing and undertake testing in accordance with statutory frameworks and best practice to ensure compliance with regulatory standards.
Environmental Impact Assessment: Carry out environmental impact assessments, delivering on assigned tasks to ensure comprehensive evaluation.
Solutions Analysis: Interpret data and identify possible answers. Involves navigating a wide variety of processes, procedures, and precedents.
Insights and Reporting: Contribute to the preparation of various data and analytics reports.
Bid Solicitation/Request for Proposal/Tender Preparation: Gather information and resources, and draft and complete standard requests for bid solicitation requests for proposal (RFP) and requests for tender (RFT) on the requester side.
Community of Practice Management: Participate actively in a community of practice in a defined area of expertise or consulting to build own expertise.
Environmental Risk Management: Coordinate the process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating environmental risks.

Education

Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering, Geology, Natural Resources, Environmental Science or equivalent.

Experience

Minimum 3 years professional experience post graduation including field sampling work
Field work will be requires
Ability to travel over night

As a multicultural organization, we encourage individual achievement and recognize the strength of a diverse workforce. GHD is an equal opportunity employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified employees and applicants without regard to race, creed, religion, national origin, citizenship, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, marital status or veteran status.

Salary Range $67,500-$116,000 based on experience and location

We'll give you control over your career, empower you to find innovative solutions and help you create a lasting impact.

See where your commitment could take you with GHD.

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

new_jobs.title: Watershed Specialist
new_jobs.description:
[Accepting submissions until 8/28. Position description has been modified to meet word count, please visit our website for full description and application link]

Cannabis for Conservation (CFC) is a 501(c)(3) environmental nonprofit that conserves, restores, and educates rural landowners with ecological tools and resources. We turn yesterday's impacts into tomorrow's solutions. From eroding roads to fire-prone forests and from exhausted soils to struggling salmon-bearing streams, we partner with cultivators, landowners, and communities to restore functional and biodiverse agroecosystems, protect clean water, and strengthen resilience to wildfire and climate change.

We are seeking to hire a Watershed Specialist with a strong field background and several years of professional experience in geology, hydrology, environmental science, forestry, civil engineering, natural resources, and project coordination. This role will strengthen CFC's ability to assess rural roads and watershed conditions, develop conceptual sediment reduction treatments, and support implementation across Humboldt, Trinity, and Mendocino Counties. The right candidate will understand how soil, water, gravity, and rural roads interact on steep, wet landscapes, how to work with a variety of stakeholders including rural landowners, a diverse organizational staff, funders, and agency representatives.

To apply, please read the full position description and application process on our website
(www.cannabisforconservation.org/careers) by clicking the "Apply" button above and submitting your materials through the application linked on our site. Questions or issues with the application process may be sent to: vanessa@cannabisforconservation.org.

Position Overview

The Watershed Specialist supports CFC’s watershed restoration and sediment reduction projects through field assessment, planning, and project and partner coordination. Core duties include assessing rural and forest roads to identify erosion and sediment sources, estimating sediment loads, evaluating hydrologic connectivity, and developing treatment recommendations. The role combines field work with office-based reporting, permitting support, and coordination with staff, landowners, and subcontractors.

This position typically works across several concurrent, landscape-scale, multi-year, multi-parcel grant projects — helping track deliverables and milestones, keep technical and field components aligned with grant requirements, and support communication with landowners and subcontractors. The Specialist also supports engineering design through field data collection and contributes to implementation through construction oversight and inspections, in collaboration with the Watershed Program Manager and the contracted Engineer of Record.

This is not an entry-level position
. The successful candidate will bring several years of relevant field-based experience in road assessment, sediment reduction, and watershed restoration planning.

Required Skills

Bachelor’s degree in geology, hydrology, civil engineering, environmental science, forestry, natural resources, or a related field
5+ years of relevant professional experience in restoration, forestry, hydrology, geology, or a related field
Strong technical background and applicable field skills; ability to conduct field assessments of roads, culverts, ditch relief features, gullies, and other erosion and sediment sources, applying strong field assessment skills to identify erosion processes, drainage patterns, hydrologic connectivity, and sediment delivery mechanisms
Collect GPS points/tracks, photos, and field sketches using ArcGIS Field Maps, and apply basic working knowledge of ArcGIS for data collection and assessment
Evaluate planning-level feasibility of standard rural road treatments (rolling dips, outsloping/insloping, critical dips, ditch relief culverts, rock armoring, culvert sizing for fish passage and 100-year flow) and apply erosion hazard rating criteria to prioritize treatment sites
Working knowledge of watercourse classification (Class I/II/III perennial, intermittent, and ephemeral streams) and its permitting implications
Familiarity with the Handbook for Forest Ranch and Rural Roads (Pacific Watershed Associates) and road-related sediment source inventory / erosion hazard rating methodologies

Description

PURPOSE

The work of the District’s Environmental Services Department centers on supporting the District’s efforts to achieve its mission to manage, protect, conserve and enhance the region's water supply in an environmentally balanced manner. The Environmental Scientist/ Regulatory Affairs Specialist provides expertise in the realm of regulatory compliance to guide and complete projects that support the District’s environmental and conservation initiatives and functions intended to achieve the District’s mission and ensure long-term sustainability of the District’s water resources programs. Primary responsibilities center on the regulatory and compliance components of the District’s projects. This includes playing both a lead and support role in the project planning, management, and implementation process for large, complex, and technical projects that are highly specialized in the water resource management sector.

Examples of Duties

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Provide technical expertise and guidance during project planning and development phase. Prepare project-specific documentation (e.g., regulatory application packages, implementation reports, and associated correspondence).
Advise District staff, Board of Directors, and executive management on regulatory and technical matters for District projects to ensure that sound science and regulatory compliance requirements are informing decisions in support of achieving the District’s mission.
Represent the District on regulatory and permitting matters to governmental agencies, various organizations, and the general public; and develop effective working relationships with representatives of key agencies and organizations.
Guide state and federal environmental review (e.g., CEQA, NEPA, cultural) and permitting (e.g., ESA, CESA, Clean Water Act, LSA, FERC license requirements) processes to support the District’s development, implementation, and operation of water resources projects.
Perform administrative tasks, as required, of the Environmental Services Department, including developing and managing contracts with consultants, developing and tracking budgets, grant applications and management, preparing reports and presentations for Board meetings, and maintaining records on project activities and the District’s compliance with requirements of federal, state, and local environmental laws, rules, and regulations.
May supervise or direct the work of other staff in the Environmental Services Department.

Typical Qualifications

EMPLOYMENT QUALIFICATIONS

Knowledge Of

Federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations along with the functions, procedures and organization of state and federal governmental agencies that administer these laws, including familiarity with the Endangered Species Act, the California Endangered Species Act, FERC licensing and compliance, Clean Water Act permitting, Lake and Streambed Alteration agreements, the California Environmental Quality Act, and the National Environmental Policy Act.
Principles of ecology, biology, hydrology, geomorphology, and water resource management.
Scientific methods and techniques of data collection, management, and analysis for ecological studies.
Preparation of formal documents including reports, letters, presentations, application packages, and other clearly written professional communication.
Principles and practices of management for projects, contracts, and budgets.
Current technology, field equipment, and computers necessary to perform work tasks.

Ability To

Manage projects to ensure that they are completed on schedule and within budget.
Apply principles of logic and scientific thinking to a wide range of intellectual and practical problems.
Read, analyze, and interpret complex documents and data.
Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.
Develop, review, and edit reports, correspondence and other technical documents.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with District staff, Board of Directors, outside agencies, and the public.

Desirable Experience And Knowledge (not Required)

Oncorhynchus mykiss biology and monitoring techniques
Dreissenid mussel biology
Invasive species management
Stream ecology
Limnology
Native flora and fauna of the Santa Clara River watershed
Biological resource survey and monitoring techniques
Plant and wildlife identification
ESA Section 7 and/or Section 10 Habitat Conservation Plans
Cultural experience
Avoidance, minimization, and mitigation measures
Water resources management
Proficiency with GIS
Proficiency with data analysis software such as R
Database management and streamlining techniques
Grant experience
Leadership experience

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in an environmental-related field (e.g., biology, environmental studies, fisheries science, water science, etc.). Masters degree is highly desirable.
A minimum of 4-6 years of experience with environmental, regulatory, and permitting matters relevant to the operation of water resource facilities.
Experienced in CEQA and NEPA planning processes including the development of CEQA and NEPA documents. Experienced in project management and state and federal environmental permitting including Clean Water Act Section 404 and 401, ESA, CESA, Fish and Game Code, and FERC license requirements. Understanding of and demonstrated ability to navigate state, regional, and local regulation processes.

CERTIFICATIONS AND LICENSES

Possession of a valid California Class C Driver’s License is required upon hire.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Requirements

Work is performed both indoors and outdoors. Outdoor conditions may include rain, high winds, and unusually high or low regional temperatures and exposure to outside elements. While performing the duties of this job, the employee may also be occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts and high, precarious places. The following are additional requirements of the position:

Mobility: Job tasks are varied and require standing, walking (sometimes on uneven terrain), sitting, climbing, bending, stooping, kneeling, and crawling.
Lifting: frequent lifting up to 20 pounds; occasional lifting up to 60 pounds.
Vision: constant use of overall vision, including near vision, distance vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus. Ability to work in front of a computer screen for several hours at a time.
Dexterity: occasional grasping, fine manipulation, reaching, pushing, and pulling; occasional use of touch to distinguish or identify objects.
Hearing/Talking: frequent hearing and talking, in person and on the phone.
Emotional/Psychological: frequent contact with coworkers and others; depending on assignment, may also frequently work alone. The employee is also expected to respond in emergency situations.
Environmental: exposure to moderate noise levels, but hearing protection must be worn in certain areas; frequent exposure to chemicals; occasionally uses smell to distinguish or identify objects.

We offer a complete benefits package to exempt professionals including health care, dental, vision, retirement, deferred compensation plans, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, holidays, vacation, and sick leave.

Exempt employees are also eligible for annual administrative leave.

The Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist is responsible for leading and managing all EHS programs within a lithium-ion battery manufacturing environment. This is a hands-on, standalone role requiring a self-motivated professional who can independently develop, implement, and maintain safety and environmental compliance programs while supporting daily manufacturing operations. The EHS Specialist will ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, DOT, and local regulatory requirements, with specific focus on chemical handling, lithium battery safety, hazardous waste management, and industrial risk prevention.

Key responsibilities

Serve as the primary EHS representative for the facility and the on-site safety resource.
Develop, implement, and continuously improve EHS policies, procedures, and training programs.
Promote a proactive safety culture across manufacturing, warehouse, and engineering teams.

Regulatory Compliance

Ensure full compliance with OSHA, EPA, state/local regulations, and industry best practices.
Maintain required EHS documentation including SDS management, incident logs, inspections, and permits.
Support regulatory audits and serve as the main contact for external agencies.

Manufacturing & Chemical Safety

Oversee safe handling and storage of lithium-ion battery materials, including electrolytes, solvents, and powders.
Implement controls for fire prevention, thermal runaway risks, and emergency response procedures.
Conduct job hazard analyses (JHAs) and risk assessments for production activities.

Compliance & audit readiness

Ensure document control practices support compliance with ISO 9001, AS9100 (if applicable), and internal ALE quality system requirements.
Support EHS-related documentation aligned with ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 where applicable.
Maintain controlled records in an audit-ready state with complete approval and traceability history.
Support internal, customer, and external audits by providing controlled documents and records promptly.

Hazardous Materials & Waste Management

Manage hazardous waste programs including labeling, storage, accumulation areas, and disposal coordination.
Ensure compliance with DOT requirements for shipping lithium batteries and hazardous materials (UN 3480/3481).
Coordinate environmental reporting and waste reduction initiatives.

Training & Employee Engagement

Conduct EHS onboarding and recurring training (PPE, chemical safety, lockout/tagout, emergency response, etc.).
Lead safety meetings, toolbox talks, and incident prevention initiatives.
Provide hands-on coaching to employees on safe work practices

Incident Management & Continuous Improvement

Lead investigations for near-misses, injuries, spills, or safety events.
Track corrective and preventive actions to closure.
Monitor site safety performance metrics and recommend improvements.

Emergency Preparedness

Maintain emergency response plans including fire protection, chemical spill response, evacuation procedures, and first aid readiness.
Coordinate drills and ensure emergency equipment is inspected and functional.

Daily On-the-Floor Support

Perform routine safety inspections and audits in production and warehouse areas.
Partner closely with operations leadership to address safety concerns in real time.
Support implementation of 5S and safe manufacturing practices.

Qualification

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, or related field (or equivalent experience).
3+ years of EHS experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Strong working knowledge of OSHA regulations and safety management systems.
Ability to work independently in a one-person EHS role and manage multiple priorities.
Experience in lithium-ion battery, chemical, electronics, or high-tech manufacturing.
Knowledge of hazardous material shipping and storage regulations (DOT/IATA).
Familiarity with ISO 14001 or ISO 45001 standards.
HAZWOPER or other relevant certifications (a plus).

Work Environment and Physical requirements

Manufacturing facility with exposure to chemicals, powered industrial equipment, and regulated battery materials.
Requires use of PPE and adherence to strict safety protocols.
May involve occasional lifting, walking production floors, and responding to urgent safety needs.
Frequent bending, squatting, reaching, and climbing.
Ability to lift up to 35 lbs.
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
Ability to work safely

We are genuinely and strongly committed to cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and connectedness where we can grow and learn together with a diverse team of employees. In recruiting team members, we welcome the unique contributions that you can bring to us and the work we do.

Job Description and Duties

This position supports CDPH’s mission and strategic plan by enhancing emergency preparedness and response goals for natural disasters and hazardous materials releases, with a particular emphasis on environmental exposures and health implications.

The Staff Toxicologist (Specialist) is a member of a multidisciplinary team and acts as a subject matter expert in toxicology, providing scientific evaluations, exposure and risk assessments, and technical work relating to toxicological exposures that result from environmental or occupational emergencies. This requires coordination with federal, state, local, territorial, and tribal agencies, as well as other relevant stakeholders to develop risk reduction measures and technical guidance. During an emergency activation, the incumbent works effectively and cooperatively under stress and pressure with short notice, and may be required to work irregular hours, weekends, holidays, or extended shifts in the field.

Experience working cooperatively with outside agencies and diverse partners

Responsibilities

The Department of Resource Management is a comprehensive agency comprised of the Environmental Health Services, Building and Safety, Planning Services, Public Works, Parks and Administrative Services Divisions. new_jobs.description:
South Coast Aqmd And Job Overview

ABOUT SOUTH COAST AQMD

South Coast Air Quality Management District (South Coast AQMD) is one of the largest and most technologically sophisticated environmental regulatory agencies in the nation, serving a four-county region that includes Los Angeles, Orange County, Riverside and San Bernardino counties, and the Coachella Valley. South Coast AQMD's headquarters is located in Diamond Bar, 30 miles east of downtown Los Angeles, at the junction of the 57 and 60 Freeways. With a highly diverse "Clean Air Team" of over 870 employees, an annual budget of $225.2 million, and a state-of-the art air quality laboratory, our mission is to ensure clean air and a healthy environment. South Coast AQMD is an organization you can be proud to work for -- we make a difference in the quality of life in Southern California!

South Coast AQMD is committed to creating and maintaining a work environment that appreciates the unique backgrounds, skills, and experiences of our employees and fosters professional development and growth. South Coast AQMD respects the ideas and perspectives of our stakeholders and works to bring them together toward the common goal of clean air.

About Our Laboratory

South Coast AQMD's laboratory employs over 40 staff in a 20,000 square foot state-of-the-art facility dedicated to air quality sample analysis. It provides a broad array of services generating actionable data that is used for strategic planning, investigating complaints from the community, evaluating new products and processes, supporting incident responses and determining compliance with regulations. We also provide data to the California Air Resources Board, US EPA, law enforcement agencies, and universities. Results generated by the laboratory have been the catalyst for agency-wide policy decisions, special studies, and technology development. We analyze over 60,000 samples per year using various analytical laboratory techniques; including GC, IC, LC, GC-MS, XRF, XRD, FTIR, microscopic analysis, ICP-MS, and PTR-MS to generate detailed information on the types and amount of pollutants in ambient air. The South Coast AQMD laboratory is at the forefront of method development for ambient air analyses and obtains national recognition in the field of air quality analytical chemistry.

About This Position

The South Coast AQMD is seeking qualified candidates to fill a Principal Air Quality Chemist vacancy. From this recruitment process, we expect to establish an eligible list from which current and future vacancies may be filled, during the 6–12-month life of the list.

Principal Chemists are expected to have expertise in many analytical techniques, data analysis, and to supervise the work of staff in their respective group. Therefore, the most competitive candidates for this position will bring a strong combination of education, atmospheric and analytical chemistry training and experience, broad knowledge of QA/QC procedures, and supervisory skills and readiness. This position will be responsible for oversight of the South Coast AQMD laboratory's Advanced Spectrometry and Microscopy groups. The primary role of the Advanced Spectrometry Principal Chemist is to help with community monitoring needs under several South Coast AQMD programs, including AB 617 (Community Air Toxics Monitoring), incident response, rule development and support, and special monitoring projects using a mobile Proton-Transfer-Reaction-Time-of-Flight-Mass Spectrometer (PTR-MS) and other advanced instrumentation.

The Principal Air Quality Chemist is a supervisory position reporting to the Laboratory Manager. This vacant position is one of four Principal positions making up the laboratory supervisory team; each team consists of eight to sixteen chemists, technicians, and support staff. Teams are aligned by function, including compliance analysis, ambient VOC/toxics analysis, aerosol analysis, and advanced spectrometry/microscopy.

EXAMPLE OF DUTIES

The general Example of Duties for this classification are highlighted below, for full description of duties please refer to this link here .

Plans, organizes, and supervises the work of staff assigned to a laboratory section involved in qualitative and quantitative analyses to isolate, identify, and quantify air contaminants; reviews requests for analyses, determines the level of difficulty, and assigns work; and provides technical and administrative guidance to professional and technical staff and evaluates performance.
Develops, supervises, prioritizes, and evaluates programs and projects; maintains workload statistics on unit activities; prepares program- and activity-related reports and analyses; reviews and edits technical reports prepared by laboratory staff to ensure accuracy of data, appropriateness of methodologies, and soundness of findings and conclusions; and identifies and maintains data quality objectives on a program basis.
Serves as a technical expert and resource for South Coast AQMD staff regarding chemistry-related air quality matters and on a variety of technical advisory committees; maintains a broad understanding of current research into causes, sources, and chemical reactions contributing to air quality problems; and consults with outside experts regarding air quality issues relevant to laboratory programs and projects.
Applies professional training and experience and keeps abreast of updated and new chemical laboratory methods, instrumentation, protocols, and practices through review of professional literature and other research resources and evaluates staff recommendations to ensure the laboratory uses the most effective and up-to-date techniques in analyzing air contaminants, accomplishing the work of the unit, and meeting new or changing South Coast AQMD rules.
Reviews and approves test methods used by private laboratories for compliance with South Coast AQMD rules.
Represents South Coast AQMD at scientific conferences and prepares for publication and presents research reports and papers on methods, procedures, results, and conclusions relating to laboratory analyses.
Testifies in court and before public bodies and hearing boards.
Prepares annual budget request for the section and submits written justification for budget items requested; and is responsible for the preparation of grant proposals for federal government or other funding.
Acts for the laboratory services manager, as needed.

Desirable Qualifications

MINIMUM AND DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

In addition to the Minimum Qualifications which follow, the most competitive candidates will also possess:

Experience with the measurement of Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) in ambient air, and the analysis, interpretation, and presentation of resultant data sets.
Experience with mobile measurements and/or field studies using research grade instrumentation, particularly mass spectrometry techniques such as PTR-MS and spectroscopic methods such as CRDS and TILDAS; along with other analytical techniques for the measurement of ambient gases and particles.
Experience with microscopic analysis for asbestos and other ambient particulate matter using polarized light microscopy, electron microscopy with EDS, XRD, FTIR, and other techniques.
Knowledge of QA/QC procedures and guidelines to ensure data is accurate and representative of the samples being collected following proper documentation procedures.
Detailed knowledge of matters directly related to ambient air analysis, laboratory instrumentation and data management.
Exceptional leadership, oral presentation, and written communication skills.
Experience overseeing the work of laboratory professionals and support staff.
Ability to identify and resolve complex programmatic and administrative challenges in a fair, impartial, and professional manner.
Ability to implement and track the progress of programs and innovative solutions to improve efficiency and productivity.
Ability to conceptualize mobile monitoring and field data using GIS based visualizations.
Ability to manage workloads to ensure timely turnaround of sample analysis and data collected during field measurements.
Ability to lead teams operating field instrumentation, both stationary and mobile, that is used extensively for monitoring pollutants near facilities and in nearby communities as well as for incident response.
Ability to oversee contracts for monitoring studies along with collaborating with researchers at universities and other agencies.
Ability to present technical data to various stakeholders having a wide range of scientific and professional backgrounds.
Strong computer and data review skills for large complex datasets that harmonize data from several instruments often with different time resolutions.
Flexibility, dependability, and a positive, can-do attitude.

Minimum Qualifications

EDUCATION:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree in chemistry, preferably with an emphasis in qualitative and quantitative analysis.

Experience

One (1) year as a Senior Air Quality Chemist or equivalent (One year working as a Manager, Supervisor, Senior Chemist, or similar leadership position that oversees a group of chemists focused on air quality measurements and/or research)

OR

Three (3) years as an Air Quality Chemist or equivalent (Three years working as a Chemist conducting air quality analysis).

KNOWLEDGE OF:
Current methods, procedures, protocols, and instrumentation relating to organic, inorganic, and physical qualitative and quantitative analysis; operational principles of relevant chemical laboratory instrumentation and techniques; principles and practices of project management, supervision, training, and budgeting; relevant professional research literature and resources; principles and methods of statistical analysis; working knowledge of database design, information management, and computer programming, as they relate to laboratory analysis of air contaminants; safety procedures and practices relating to laboratory work; PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; professional report writing; South Coast AQMD rules and federal and State laws related to chemical analysis of air contaminants; and protocols and standards for laboratory analysis of air quality samples.

SKILL OR ABILITY TO:
Supervise, evaluate, train, and assign work to professional and technical staff involved in routine and complex qualitative and quantitative organic, inorganic and physical analysis of air quality samples; effectively use available resources in planning and organizing programs and projects; evaluate the effectiveness of programs and projects in meeting laboratory and overall South Coast AQMD objectives; oversee the development and implementation of new laboratory methods, procedures, and protocols, the adaptation of existing instrumentation and methods for new purposes, and the evaluation of new instrumentation; understand and interpret applicable laws, rules, and regulations; edit and write detailed, accurate reports on laboratory projects, analyses, methodologies, findings, and conclusions; prepare funding proposals; read, understand, and follow verbal and written directions; proficiently use PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; and establish and maintain effective relationships with all those contacted in the course of work.

LICENSE:
Possession of a valid California Class "C" Driver's License and a good driving record may be required.

Other Important Information

APPLICATION PACKETS MUST INCLUDE

A completed employment application covering at least the past 10 years of employment history (or longer if you have other relevant experience), and your entire South Coast AQMD employment history if you are a South Coast AQMD employee.

Company Description

Location:
Bend, Oregon

Schedule:
Full-Time | Onsite

Join a Global Leader in Sustainable Agriculture

At Suterra, we're changing the future of agriculture through science-based, environmentally responsible pest management solutions. As the global leader in pheromone technology, we help growers protect crops while reducing the use of conventional pesticides.

We're looking for a Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Analyst
to join our Global Regulatory Affairs team at our headquarters in Bend, Oregon.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone early in their regulatory or environmental compliance career who wants to gain hands-on experience working with federal and state regulatory requirements, environmental reporting, and product compliance in a collaborative manufacturing environment.

You'll work closely with Manufacturing, Operations, Quality, R&D, Supply Chain, and Commercial teams to help ensure our products and operations remain compliant while supporting innovative technologies used around the world.

This position is based full-time in Bend, Oregon. Regular onsite collaboration is an essential part of this role. Remote or hybrid work arrangements are not available. Relocation to the Bend area is required for candidates who do not currently reside locally.

Job Description

What You'll Do

As a Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Analyst, you'll support the day-to-day regulatory and environmental compliance activities that keep our products, facilities, and operations running safely and responsibly.

Responsibilities include:

Prepare and maintain environmental reports required by federal, state, and local regulatory agencies.
Support environmental permitting and compliance activities, including waste management, air emissions, hazardous materials, and chemical reporting.
Assist with regulatory submissions, product registrations, renewals, and regulatory documentation.
Maintain permits, certifications, regulatory files, and compliance records.
Monitor changes in environmental and regulatory requirements and communicate potential impacts to the business.
Support regulatory inspections, agency requests, and internal and external audits.
Partner with Manufacturing, Quality, R&D, Supply Chain, and Operations to ensure regulatory requirements are incorporated into daily operations.
Assist in developing compliance procedures, documentation, and employee training materials.
Identify opportunities to improve regulatory processes and strengthen compliance programs.

Qualifications

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources, or a related scientific field.
Approximately 2–5 years of experience in environmental compliance, regulatory affairs, EHS, environmental consulting, manufacturing compliance, or a related field.
Experience working with or preparing documentation for federal and/or state regulatory agencies such as EPA, OSHA, DEQ, ODA, or similar agencies.
Experience supporting environmental reporting, permitting, inspections, or compliance documentation.
Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accurate records and documentation.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in manufacturing, agriculture, chemical manufacturing, biotechnology, food production, or related industries.
Familiarity with pesticide, chemical, or environmental regulations.
Experience participating in regulatory inspections or compliance audits.

You'll Be Successful in This Role If You

Enjoy working with technical regulations and detailed documentation.
Like solving practical problems and finding compliant solutions.
Can build positive working relationships across multiple departments.
Are organized, dependable, and proactive.
Want to continue building your expertise in environmental and regulatory compliance.
Appreciate working in a collaborative, onsite environment.

This is more than a field service role. It's the first step in a career supporting growers, advancing sustainable agriculture, and developing technical expertise in one of California's most important industries.

Hands-on training and mentorship from experienced agricultural professionals.
Opportunities to build technical skills and grow your career.

new_jobs.description:
Senior Environmental Scientist

Brisbane or Cairns QLD

RPS, A Tetra Tech company

RPS, A Tetra Tech company, is a global professional services firm delivering projects that define, shape and manage Australia's most important infrastructure, development and environmental initiatives.

With more than 5,000 professionals across 125 countries, we bring together technical excellence, practical thinking and a collaborative approach to solve complex challenges across infrastructure, energy, water, environment, urban development and resources.

Our Oceans & Environment team partners with government and private sector clients to deliver innovative environmental solutions that support sustainable development while protecting our natural environment.

The Opportunity

Due to continued growth, we are looking for a Senior Environmental Scientist to join our Oceans & Environment team in our Brisbane or Cairns offices.

This is an exciting opportunity to work on a diverse portfolio of infrastructure, renewable energy, transport, water and development projects across Queensland and Australia. You will collaborate with experienced environmental consultants and technical specialists to deliver environmental assessments, approvals and management solutions that help clients achieve successful project outcomes.

Whether you enjoy field work, technical reporting, environmental approvals or working closely with clients, this role offers excellent variety and the opportunity to grow your career within a supportive national team.

What You Will Be Doing

Preparing environmental assessments, technical reports and environmental management plans.
Assisting with environmental impact assessments and planning approval documentation.
Conducting environmental investigations, literature reviews and data analysis.
Supporting environmental approvals under Queensland and Commonwealth legislation.
Coordinating inputs from technical specialists and project stakeholders.
Working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Building strong relationships with clients, regulators and internal stakeholders.
Assisting with project planning, budgeting and delivery to meet client expectations.
Supporting proposal preparation and business development activities.
Ensuring work is delivered safely on time and to a high technical standard.

About You

You will be passionate about delivering practical environmental outcomes and enjoy working on a wide variety of projects in a collaborative consulting environment.

You Will Also Bring

A degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
Experience working in environmental consulting, government or a related industry.
Knowledge of Queensland environmental legislation and environmental assessment processes.
An understanding of the Commonwealth Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (EPBC Act).
Strong technical report writing and communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex information clearly.
Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
A collaborative approach and a commitment to delivering quality outcomes for clients.
A current Australian driver's licence and willingness to undertake occasional field work and travel as required.

Why Join RPS?

At RPS, we believe our people are our greatest strength. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive workplace where you can develop your career while contributing to projects that create lasting value for our communities.

We Offer

Professional development and career progression opportunities
A supportive team culture that celebrates collaboration and success
Flexible working arrangements to support work-life balance
Active wellbeing and community engagement initiatives
Annual professional membership reimbursement
Paid parental and partner leave
$250 active lifestyle allowance per annum
Additional annual leave purchase scheme and salary packaging options
Professional and technical development programs, including study assistance, online learning and mentoring across portfolios
Active office social events, Employee Assistance Program, service recognition and more

Our Commitment

At RPS, everyone is empowered to bring their best. We foster a workplace where different perspectives are valued, collaboration is encouraged and people are supported to grow professionally.

As part of Tetra Tech, we combine local knowledge with global expertise to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients while creating opportunities for our people.

Ready to Make an Impact?

If you are looking to build your environmental consulting career with a respected global consultancy and work on projects that make a real difference across Queensland and beyond, we would love to hear from you.

Apply today and help shape a more sustainable future with RPS, A Tetra Tech company.

Our Approach

Our people live our purpose, deliver our promise, and demonstrate our behaviours every day. Our behaviours define who we are. Developed by our people, they underpin everything that we do. They create the memorable experiences we are known for and make RPS a great place to do great work.

Stronger together is one of our five core behaviours and it is key to building a collaborative workplace. We encourage everyone to bring their best and to support others to do the same. By sharing knowledge, challenging each other to think differently, and fostering an environment of trust and respect, our people can learn, grow and thrive – and share in our success.

Recruitment Agencies

We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on this list. Please refer to the careers page on our website if you require any further information.
